messages:
ian: noticed weird blip in the tenant quota panel for org-phi — small spike with tooltip showing org-zeta. saw it in prod console at ~09:12 UTC. anyone else? :confused:
maya: yep i caught that too while reviewing customer dashboards. quick repro: switch to org-phi, open /console/usage?range=24h -> top-right quota panel shows a ~60s spike. clicking details shows org_id: org-zeta in the hover metadata.
ian: can reproduce locally hitting the console metrics endpoint with header: 
```
curl -H \"X-ORG-ID: org-phi\" \"https://console.internal/api/v1/panels/quota?org=org-phi\" | jq '.data[] | select(.org_id!="org-phi")'
```
rachel: that pattern matches a cache-hit where cached payload contains a mismatched org tag. we rolled the prefetch key normalization last week (PR #4123). suspect key no longer includes X-ORG-ID for some codepaths.
sam: deploy history: prefetch service v2.2.1 rolled at 03:00 UTC (10% canary -> 100%). infra-bot logs show prefetch cache writes with key=pf:console:panel:/quota but no tenant suffix.
infra-bot: prefetch-write event: service=console-prefetch key=pf:console:panel:/quota, headers=[{"x-forwarded-for":"10.0.0.12"}]
maya: that confirms it. impact: tiny subset of users may see other orgs' panel datapoints. not many but still PII risk.
security: pinged. need scope: scan returned payloads for any user-identifiable fields in leaked rows. prioritize high-visibility orgs.
ian: immediate mitigation options: 1) invalidate pf:console:* for last 48h, 2) add a gateway validator that refuses to return cached entries where cached_payload.org_id != incoming X-ORG-ID (fast), 3) short rollback of prefetch normalization (slow but safe).
rachel: i can PR the gateway validator. simple check in cache middleware: if cached.org_id && cached.org_id != req.header('X-ORG-ID') -> bypass and mark metric cache_mismatch. Add unit test for cache key composition.
sam: invalidation checklist: redis prefixes to purge: pf:console:panel:*, console-prefetch-resp:*. i'll run redis-cli keys+del in maintenance window. need ops approval.
maya: let's not rollback immediately — validator + purge should reduce blast radius and we can deploy a canary e2e that asserts tenant isolation.
security: start notification to affected customers if more than 5 orgs saw leaks or any PII. also create incident ticket SEC-2026-111.
ian: opening INC-2026-49 with repro steps, logs, and mitigation plan. tagging @ops for cache purge. ETA 20m for initial invalidation.
infra-bot: Cache-prefix purge scheduled by ops user 'sam' at 09:45 UTC.
sam: purge complete. confirmed ~412 keys removed across prod cluster.
rachel: merged gateway validator (branch: feat/prefetch-tenant-assert) and deployed to canary (10%). adding integration test that simulates cached payload with mismatched org.
maya: running telemetry scan for cross-tenant matches last 14 days, results will go to #security and #cs. adding a regression alert that fires when cache_mismatch rate > 0.1% of panel requests.
security: received telemetry dump. no user emails or direct PII observed in leaked rows, but org ids exposed. recommending customer notification template and opt-in monitoring for affected orgs.
ian: follow-ups: postmortem, change logs for prefetch key design, add tenant to key composition explicitly, and add synthetic canary that runs per-deployment verifying no cross-tenant responses on a small sample of requests.
sam: thanks all. will schedule postmortem + action items in the runbook. :white_check_mark:
